newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1997 budget will be implemented - Belka.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1997 budget will be implemented - Belka.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry said on Wednesday that it will meet revenue and spending levels written into the 1997 budget, even though the budget has been strained.
"I am convinced that this year's budget will be implemented. We see no threat here even though it is a strained budget," Finance Minister Marek Belka told a news conference.

Belka earlier said Poland was now having serious problems in placing various papers on the market. He gave no details, but this was viewed as an apparent reference to placing Treasury bills and bonds on the domestic market. Analysts do not foresee lack of appetite for Polish debt issues targetting foreign investors.

Last week, the ministry said the budget gap widened by 1.61 billion zlotys in April to 5.57 billion in the first four months of the year, which accounted for 45.6 percent of the planned 1997 deficit of 12.22 billion zlotys.
Belka said the deficit will grow more slowly in the remainder of the year.
